ZERO turns start here and ZERO events. The whole fragment is one continuous stretch of the annual message of the president of the Nation (Menem) to the Legislative Assembly: it opens mid-sentence ("Tenemos la infraestructura...") and runs past the closing boundary. In the raw file data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/1999-03-01_r00_ASAMBLEA.html the governing label, printed far earlier at the head of the message under the heading "Mensajedel señor presidente de la Nación" (printed with no space after "Mensaje"), is "Sr. PRESIDENTE DE LA NACIÓN.-". None of that is inside this stretch, so nothing is listed. EVENTS RECLASSIFIED, NOT DROPPED. The fragment does contain nine italic applause/standing notes, and they are real; I first listed all nine as events, reading the brief's line that "a parenthesised note like (Aplausos.) is also an event" as independent of where the note sits. Under the corpus convention (TODO.md Phase 2, and the PDF side's inline_italic block type) an event is a note printed as its OWN paragraph, while an italic fragment inline inside a speaker's paragraph is merged back into that speech and does not split the turn. I checked all nine on the page rather than assuming: every one is inline, closing the president's own paragraph, with the next

opening his next paragraph — including the long opening one, "(Pónense de pie los legisladores. Aplausos prolongados y manifestaciones en las bancas y en las galerías.)", which follows "¡Viva la Argentina! ¡Viva Chile!" inside that same paragraph and does not stand alone. So all nine are fragments of the president's speech and the events list is empty. For the record, the eight short ones read "(Aplausos.)" as printed. The nine are typeset three different ways, which is worth knowing for any rule that keys on the italic span: five read "(Aplausos.)" with the period and both parentheses outside the italics, three read "(Aplausos.)" with the period inside, and the long standing-ovation note puts the whole thing including both parentheses inside one italic run, "(Pónense de pie...)". A parser reading the italic span alone therefore sees "Aplausos" for five, "Aplausos." for three, and a fully parenthesised string for the ninth. This fragment is lowercase HTML (

, ) with unclosed

and no wrappers at all, unlike the other two stretches I annotated, so a rule that keys on the FONT wrapper would see nothing here. No headings, no furniture, no inserted documents.
